conviction_note: Near non-result: no Q1 forecast revision expected (none at Q1 in three years), no new return expected beyond the already-guided ¥2.5 interim dividend, and the quarter's two readable lines (Q1 margin leverage from lapping last year's ad blitz, and a tougher Sansan-segment growth comparison) roughly offset. That leaves a slight negative lean from the last two Q1 prints being sold (-2.65%, -5.92%) and a +12% 20-day / +8% 5-day run-in. abs_move 4.5 sits above the 3.45 proxy because this name's own reactions on its real release dates were 4.3% median and 6.4% mean. p_up 47 gives -0.27. impact_sum (-0.1) and the scaled number agree in sign and are both close to zero.
bar: Full year: IFIS consensus (kabuyoho, 2026-10-08) of revenue ¥64,339m and OP ¥13,648m against a company range of ¥63,706-65,319m revenue and ¥12,514-14,464m OP, so consensus sits at the midpoint (https://kabuyoho.jp/sp/reportAnalyst?bcode=4443). The Q1 bar is unsourced: I found no published Q1 consensus, and Yahoo's earningsTrend returned 'Invalid Crumb'. Every quarter-level finding is therefore capped small. My own arithmetic from the company's sequential trend puts Q1 revenue near ¥14.7bn (+20% YoY), inside the guide.

findings.finding: Q1 (Jun-Aug) is Sansan's ad-heavy quarter: a new Sansan TVCM ran from 2026-05-25, as the three-product TVCM blitz ran from 2025-05-28. Last year that blitz doubled Q1 ad spend to ¥2,163m (32% of the full year's ¥6,770m) and held Q1 adjusted OP to ¥578m (6.9% of the year). This year's full-year ad budget is guided up only about 8%, so Q1 ad growth should be small against ~20% revenue growth, and Q1 adjusted OP as a share of the year should land well above last year's 6.9%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY2026 (released 2025-10-10): EPS ¥2.36 against ¥2.61 consensus on the ad blitz, next close -5.92%. Q1 FY2025 (2024-10-11): next close -2.65%.
findings.why_not_priced: The Q1 consensus is not published anywhere I could reach. If the market had priced the leverage, the stock's last two Q1 prints would not set the template for selling. But analysts have both the ad guide and the CM date, so most of this is probably modelled, which is why it is sized small.
findings.independence: TVCM start date from Sansan's own release (https://jp.corp-sansan.com/feed/, item dated 2026-05-25). The +8% ad guide is in the FY presentation (https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260713/140120260713592191.pdf). The two documents are independent of each other.

findings.finding: The Sansan (business-card) segment faces a hard Q1 comparison. Q1 FY2026 Sansan sales grew +19.3%, with other sales up +53.4% to ¥539m. Recurring sales QoQ adds slowed through FY2026 from +281 to +243, +207 and +181 (¥m), and Q4 Sansan sales grew only +11.5% (recurring +13.7%, other -14.9%). Simple extrapolation puts Q1 FY2027 Sansan growth near 10%, at the bottom of the 10-12% guide, while the stock trades on the 'AI kills SaaS' narrative.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean isolate. The two big up-moves (+17.41% on the Q2 FY2026 print of 2026-01-14, +9.14% on the FY print of 2026-07-13) came on prints without a Sansan-segment disappointment.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: anyone can compute it from the last 短信 and presentation, and it sits inside the company's own 10-12% guide. What could be new is whether Sansan's churn (0.55% L12M) or price per subscription (-1.0% YoY) worsens. A deterioration there would be visible in sell-side previews if the market already expected it, and I found none.
findings.independence: Q1 FY2026 segment table (https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20251010/140120251010571629.pdf) supplies the comparison base. It is the same company's own disclosure series, so not independent.

findings.finding: The Q1 print is structurally the quietest. Sansan has not revised its full-year forecast at any Q1 in three years (unchanged on 2023-10-12, 2024-10-11 and 2025-10-10; its only revision was at Q3, 2026-04-10). Shareholder returns are already set (¥2.5 interim dividend guided in July; the buyback ended 2026-06-18). Both prior Q1 prints were sold (-2.65%, -5.92%), and the stock comes in at +12.2% over 20 days, +8.2% over 5 days and +4.9% on the print-day morning.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 prints with no revision: -2.65% (2024-10-11 release), -5.92% (2025-10-10). The Q3 FY2026 revision (low end raised) still drew -3.55%.
findings.why_not_priced: The run-in means some holders are positioned for a beat. A print that only confirms the guide gives them no new catalyst. If this were priced, the stock would have stalled into the print rather than gaining 8% in five sessions.
findings.independence: Revision record from IFIS/kabuyoho. The release dates and next-close moves come from kabutan's disclosure list (https://kabutan.jp/stock/news?code=4443&nmode=3) and Yahoo daily bars. The run-up is the free control itself, so this finding partly agrees with the positioning.

findings.finding: Peer read: Rakus (Japanese back-office SaaS, reported 2026-08-14 for Apr-Jun) posted Q1 ordinary profit +33.2% and a 23.8% progress rate, in line with its 5-year average of 22.6%, with plan unchanged. This shows no AI-driven demand break in Japanese back-office SaaS through June.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it is two months old and public. Included as the only counterparty data point since Sansan last reported.

bar_hierarchy: Forecast revision: unlikely; none at Q1 in 3 years, and IFIS sits at the midpoint of the range. Returns: none expected (interim ¥2.5 already guided; buyback completed 2026-06-18). New-year guide: n/a, this is Q1. Quarter vs own 進捗率 history: Q1 adj OP progress was 5.8% (FY2025) and 6.9% (FY2026); with ad growth guided at +8% for the year, this Q1 should run higher, but the Q1 consensus is unsourced.
baseline_tension: The findings roughly offset. The small negative lean agrees with the run-up and priced_lean_pct (-0.34), so it is not much of an edge. The strongest positive the release could carry is a Q1 adj OP well above last year's 6.9% progress on ad-spend leverage; I looked for it and it is in finding 1. I looked for a buyback or an early revision and found neither signalled.
lessons_applied: Rule 1: the Sansan-segment deceleration rests on arithmetic anyone can do from the last 短信, so that finding went from -0.6 to -0.3 and p_up moved toward 50 (45 to 47)
Open question 4 (a five-day run-in sized as a short was wrong once): the run-up part of the Q1-template finding was cut, -0.7 to -0.4
Rule 2: negatives and positives were already balanced at two each. I checked for a held forecast, a buyback and a dividend change, and the Q1 margin-leverage positive stands unchanged at +0.5
